newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehbacher-dollar/mark rate helps German exporters.
newsitem.headline: Kuehbacher-dollar/mark rate helps German exporters.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Tuesday that the current dollar level against the mark was beneficial to German exporters but noted that the Group of Seven leading industrial nations had said they were opposed to exchange rate volatility.
"Our exporting economy can live very well with the dollar rate...But the G7 has repeatedly said that they want the exchange rate to develop calmly," Kuehbacher told a news conference.

The dollar was trading just above 1.73 marks at 1.7310/20 at 1200 GMT, helped by a three-pfennig surge in sterling against the mark after Britain's new Labour government ordered an increase in interest rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent on Tuesday.

G7 finance ministers and central bank chiefs, meeting in Washington at the end of April, issued a statement which said exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility and significant deviations from fundamentals were undesirable.
Kuehbacher added that the true value of the mark would be revealed on May 20 when the latest tax revenue estimate for 1997 will be published.
The estimate is expected to give an indication of Germany's chances of meeting the key budget deficit criterion for qualifying for Europe's planned monetary union.
Under the deficit criterion, a country must target it's budget deficit at a limit of three percent of its gross domestic product.
